Food · Designs for testing

Hunger, designed.

Chicken 65 from South India, rethought for masa totopos. A braise that borrows from two kitchens. Twelve dishes are specified for a first round of kitchen tests. None are cooked for guests. None are for sale.

NASHA is in development. There is no brewery, no restaurant, no truck and no menu for sale yet. Images are concept visualizations and illustrations, not photographs of NASHA. The drawings are proposed presentation, not our finished dishes.

Vegetarian story

Vegetarian is not a side.

Both India and Mexico have strong plant-based cooking traditions we want to learn from. NASHA designs vegetarian dishes as headliners, not substitutes.

Labels say “vegetarian as designed”. They are not a certified dietary statement; cross-contact is not assessed yet.

  • Chaat Elote — Charred corn with chile, lime and a crisp topping, intended to taste like street corn from two roadsides.
  • Dal-Frijol Dip — A slow-simmered black lentil and bean dip with a spiced-butter finish, for tearing bread and chips.
  • Gobi Taco — Crisp spiced cauliflower, tamarind-chile glaze and lime slaw in corn tortillas.
  • Paneer Tikka Taco — Charred yogurt-marinated paneer with green salsa and pineapple, intended to stay tender in a corn tortilla.
  • Toasted Seed & Chile Vegetable Bowl — Vegetables in a sauce of toasted nuts, seeds and dried chile, intended to be neither a mole nor a curry.
  • Cardamom Churros — Crisp churros dusted with cardamom sugar, with a dark jaggery-chocolate sauce.

Fire

Char, smoke, quick heat.

Tandoor-style heat and a hot comal give the food its edges. Fire is how the kitchen is designed to work, and how the beer is meant to be met.

“Fusion” means a dish we invented by combining two traditions. “Inspired by” means built from a tradition without claiming to be it. The lamb dish depends on an unresolved cut decision.

NASHA is a future Indo-Mex brewery and kitchen in Austin, Texas, in development.

The name was chosen by the founder. Legal clearance of the name is pending. Nothing here claims trademark ownership. There is no brewery, restaurant or truck open, and nothing is for sale. No site has been chosen.

In Hindi and Urdu, nasha means intoxication or addiction. We chose it for the feeling of being drawn in by food, craft and company. We take that meaning seriously and will never present excess or addiction as something to admire. Cultural advisors will review the name and our language before launch.

Images show a possible future. The photographic-style pictures are concept visualizations made with AI tools and edited, and the drawings are illustrations. They are not photographs of NASHA, of its food, or of its beer. About these images.

Menu items are designs for testing, not served food. Heat and vegetarian labels describe how a dish is designed, not a certified allergen or dietary statement. Ask before you eat if you have an allergy. If you drink, drink responsibly. Alcohol is for adults of legal drinking age.

The word NASHA in the header and in some pictures is a temporary typographic placeholder, set in a standard font. It is not a logo, not an official brand mark, and no trademark is claimed. No logo has been approved or released.
